name: MWE Havoc Championship
notes: Named in the fed's own Adrenaline Rush results (board topic 7556801, "Havok Title Match"), in the pre-match roleplays for it (board topics 7553106 and 7554081) and across the roleplays of early 2009. The championship ledger, board topic 7550985, covers five other belts and not this one.
epitaph: A hardcore-division belt the fed's own championship ledger never covered. It was decided in an Inferno match between JJ Executioner and Milenko at Adrenaline Rush on 28 December 2008, with Executioner promising in his own roleplay to be the first Havoc Champion. By the following January it was in Eric Derf's hands alongside the X-Television title, and Alex Bowen spent the spring of 2009 saying in public that he intended to reclaim a belt he refused to see laid to rest. No ledger of its reigns survives.

name: MWE Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: A belt whose whole recorded lineage runs across four months. Sonny Williams beat Vega Knight for it on 12 December 2008, on the final edition of Friday Night Genesis. Zak Warner took it from him on the 26 January 2009 Monday Night Mayhem, and Paige beat Warner for it at Highway to Hell on 29 March 2009. The ledger then listed it vacant, to be decided at Tribulation — and at Tribulation on 24 May 2009 it was: Sinc Mercier won a Scavenger Hunt match to unify it with the United States Championship under his own name, and this title's own reign ledger ends there. See the United States Championship's own epitaph for the unified lineage onward.

name: MWE Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The belt MWE crowded most: its first recorded champions, Project Revolution, won it at Turmoil in a six-team match, and the pair who took it from them, Maxxamillion Mustafa and the Grand Mystique, won it the same way. Darius and Boyd beat the Hollywood Hooligans for it on the 24 November 2008 Genesis, lost it to Project Revolution on the 12 January 2009 Monday Night Mayhem — a match the fed booked as a unification with a separate World Tag Team Championship — and the belts passed to Tex-Mex that March and to the Black List Mafia at Highway to Hell on 29 March 2009. The fed billed them the Undisputed MWE Tag Team Championships from the unification onward. Black List Mafia never lost the belts in the ring: Leon Roberts vacated them himself on 22 June 2009 to chase the vacant United States Championship instead, and no further reign is held in the held record.

name: MWE Undisputed Championship
notes: The fed's own championship ledger (board topic 7550985, "Championship Histories") heads this lineage "MWE Undisputed Championship History" while its show scripts bill the same belt as the MWE World Heavyweight Championship, the MWE World Championship and the MWE Championship interchangeably; both billings are recorded rather than one resolved into the other. Between the November 2008 brand draft and the Adrenaline Rush II unification the fed staged a second, Genesis-exclusive world title, won by D.C. on the 12 December 2008 Genesis and absorbed into this one — the ledger records no separate reign history for it.
epitaph: The promotion's own top belt. David Whitman won it in a ten-man battle royal at Crowning Glory II on 10 August 2008 and lost it, reclaimed it and lost it again across the next four months, to Sonny Williams at Turmoil and to Brian Michaels on a December Monday Night Mayhem. At Adrenaline Rush II on 28 December 2008, in a Three Stages of Hell match at Madison Square Garden, D.C. beat Michaels to unify the MWE Championship and the World Championship into a single Undisputed Championship. Whitman took it back in a triple threat two weeks later and held it into the summer of 2009, billed at Tribulation that May the longest-reigning champion in MWE history — two apparent losses along the way, to Ace Cannon in March and to Joseph Sharpman in May, both controversial finishes the fed's own text and its own on-air ruling declined to recognize as title changes. His real, final loss came on 8 June 2009, to Sinc Mercier in a Triple Threat also involving Kevin Hardaway. Mercier held it at least into that August, retaining at Independence Day and, after an overturned double-DQ, at Crowning Glory.

name: MWE United States Championship
epitaph: MWE's secondary singles belt, and the one its ledger records changing hands most often. Sinc Mercier beat James Sullivan for it at MWE Turmoil on 14 September 2008. Alejandro Rodriguez took it from him at Wrestle Wars II that October in a three-way with Mason Resoan and was stripped of it once the fed reviewed the tape of the finish. Mercier won it back that November, lost it to Resoan at Adrenaline Rush II and beat him for it again at Friday Night Overdrive on 13 February 2009 in a Ladder Match. The ledger then recorded it vacant, to be decided at Tribulation; the belt was still being defended in Shattered Glass and Iron Man Table matches through the year, Mason Resoan and Leon Roberts fighting for the vacant title at Independence Day that July. At Tribulation on 24 May 2009, Sinc Mercier won a Scavenger Hunt match to unify this belt with the Intercontinental Championship under his own name — his fourth US title, his first IC title, both at once.

name: MWE Women's Championship
notes: Named in the fed's own Crowning Glory II Hall of Fame segment (board topic 574107), its Tribulation 2009 induction segment (board topic 7631072) and Paige's own roster card (board topic 7550706). The championship ledger, board topic 7550985, does not cover it.
epitaph: The fed's own women's belt, remembered on screen rather than recorded in its ledger. Katherine Tenaud was its first champion, named as such in the Hall of Fame ceremony that opened MWE's relaunch in August 2008 and again at Tribulation the following May, where the fed called her the only woman in its history to win a title that was not this one. Paige is billed a former holder on her own roster card. No ledger of its reigns survives.

name: X-Television Championship
epitaph: MWE's own junior-division belt, and the only one in its ledger to pass through a mask. Aeron Beowulf beat J.K. Valentino for it at Crowning Glory II on 10 August 2008; Vega Knight took it that October and was stripped of it on being drafted to Genesis. A tournament final at Adrenaline Rush II settled it as a Mask vs Career match between the masked Mysterious G and Samuel Steele, and the winner pulled his own mask off afterwards to reveal Eric Derf. Anderson surrendered the belt on air that May rather than defend it, and the fed's own text records no result for the "NEW, and PROPER Champion" match Dick Malibu promised in its place. The belt was still being defended at the October 2009 Turmoil.
